# Phase 5 — Build Plan

Sequenced implementation of the [parallel-orchestration design](design-parallel-orchestration.md).
Each phase has a **definition of done** and the **tests that prove it**. We checkpoint at every
phase boundary for review; CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs `pytest src/aitk/tests/` on every
PR as the automatic gate.

**Ground rule:** acceptance tests for each phase are **hand-written** (never generated by the
code under test) — the same ground-truth principle the benchmarks use.

---

## Phase 5.1 — Node-spec schema (the contract) ✅ done

Everything downstream reads or writes node specs, so the schema lands first.

**Build:** `src/aitk/plan.py` — a `NodeSpec` model, `parse_node_spec()`, plan-level
`validate_plan()`, topological ordering, and write-scope overlap detection. Extend
`docs/spec-format.md` with the node-spec frontmatter.

**Node-spec fields:** `id`, `language`, `frameworks`, `depends_on`, `output_scope`,
`acceptance_criteria` (with ids), `validation_kind` (`automated` | `gated`), `test_command`,
`estimated_lines`.

**Definition of done / tests:**
- Parse a node spec file → `NodeSpec` with all fields (`test_plan.py`).
- Acceptance criteria normalize from both plain-string and `{id, text}` forms; ids unique.
- `validate_plan` flags: duplicate node ids, `depends_on` to unknown id, dependency cycles,
  bad `validation_kind`, duplicate criterion ids.
- `topological_levels` returns correct dependency levels; independent nodes share a level.
- Scope-overlap detection catches file==file, file-under-dir, and dir-prefix collisions.

---

## Phase 5.2 — `plan` / `build` CLI split + approval gate

**Build:** `aitk plan --spec <main> --out .aitk/plans/<feature>/` emits node specs to disk and
halts. `aitk build --plan .aitk/plans/<feature>/` consumes the approved (optionally
human-edited) plan. Planner = tiered (context-gatherer + structured-DAG API call; agent only on
`needs_exploration`).

**Definition of done / tests:**
- `plan` writes one `<node-id>.md` per node and a plan manifest; exits without generating code.
- `build` loads the plan, validates it (5.1), refuses an invalid/cyclic plan.
- Planner output validated against the DAG schema; `needs_exploration` path is exercised by a stub.
- Human edits to on-disk node specs are picked up by `build`.

---

## Phase 5.3 — Single-node executor (multi-file leaf)

**Build:** extract `generate.py`'s loop into a node executor that handles a **multi-file** node:
worker → tester (with acceptance-criteria coverage check) → reviewer, bounded retry loop.
Pluggable test runner via `test_command`; `gated` nodes skip automated tests.

**Definition of done / tests:**
- Executes a node, writes its file set to an isolated sandbox dir.
- Deterministic acceptance-criteria coverage check fails fast on an uncovered criterion and
  loops back to the tester (no Claude call spent).
- Reviewer receives criteria + coverage map; `gated` nodes route to the review/human gate.
- Result store extracts signatures + docstrings from the node's files.

---

## Phase 5.4 — The broker (dollar ledger + write-scope leases)

**Build:** a durable, cross-process broker. Dollar-budget token bucket (refuse/queue past the
cap) and atomic whole-scope write-leases with TTL/heartbeat.

**Definition of done / tests:**
- Cumulative spend tracked in dollars; calls past the ceiling are refused/queued.
- Atomic whole-scope acquisition; overlapping scopes serialize; non-overlapping run concurrently.
- A lease whose heartbeat lapses (simulated crash) is reclaimed.
- Two separate processes coordinate through the broker (integration test).

---

## Phase 5.5 — The DAG scheduler

**Build:** bounded-concurrency DAG executor on top of the broker — many planners' nodes
interleaved, ready-set drained, dependents released on success. Failure policy is a **pluggable
hook** (default decided here, per the parked decision).

**Definition of done / tests:**
- No-edge DAG runs all nodes concurrently up to the bound; edged DAG respects order.
- Two planners' nodes interleave under one budget.
- Scope conflicts serialize even across planners.
- Failure-policy hook is invoked on a hard-failed node.

---

## Scope gate: what gets built, and when

The design below 5.3 is large relative to what exists. To avoid building infrastructure ahead of
evidence, the plan is split into two tiers:

**Tier 1 — build now (small, independently useful):** 5.1 schema ✅, 5.2 `plan`/`build` CLI,
5.3 single-node executor. Together these give a human-approved, multi-file, sequential build that
runs end to end. A sequential in-process runner over `topological_levels()` is enough to ship it.

**Tier 2 — build only when justified:** 5.4 broker and 5.5 scheduler. Their trigger is *measured*,
not assumed. Proceed only if the benchmark baseline (see the roadmap's "Next Up" section) shows at
least one of:
- real runs are wall-clock bound and independent nodes could run concurrently, or
- Claude rate limits (429s) are actually hit, or
- parallel runs collide on files in practice.

Until then, a simple in-process dollar-budget counter and `asyncio.gather` over a level cover the
need at a fraction of the complexity (no cross-process lease store, no heartbeat/TTL machinery).
